question: When does the kubelet pull an image again instead of using the cached one?

relevant.section: Images > Updating images

reference_answer: It depends on `imagePullPolicy`. `IfNotPresent`: pull only if the image isn't already present locally. `Always`: each time a container starts, the kubelet asks the registry for the image digest and pulls only if that exact digest isn't cached. `Never`: never pull. If the policy is omitted and the tag is `:latest` (or there is no tag), the default is `Always`.

question: How do I see the current CPU and memory usage of my pods?
reference_answer: `kubectl top pod`; it needs the Metrics Server running in the cluster.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07) | human review v2 batch 3 (Youssef Zemzem, 2026-11-07): added the kubectl top pod page

question: How do I switch kubectl between two clusters?

relevant.section: Configure Access to Multiple Clusters > Define clusters, users, and contexts

reference_answer: Define clusters, users and contexts in a kubeconfig file, then switch with `kubectl config use-context <context>` (the documented example: `kubectl config --kubeconfig=config-demo use-context dev-frontend`).
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07) | human review v2 batch 3 (Youssef Zemzem, 2026-11-07): aligned with the documented command

question: How do I check whether a Deployment rollout has finished?

relevant.section: Deployments > Updating a Deployment
Deployments > Deployment status

reference_answer: `kubectl rollout status deployment/<name>`.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: How can I preview what applying a manifest would change in the cluster?

relevant.section: kubectl Quick Reference > Compares the current state of the cluster against the state that the cluster would be in if the manifest was applied.

reference_answer: `kubectl diff -f ./my-manifest.yaml`.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Should I create ReplicaSets directly or use Deployments?

relevant.section: ReplicaSet > When to use a ReplicaSet

reference_answer: Use Deployments: a Deployment manages ReplicaSets and provides declarative updates to Pods. Create a ReplicaSet directly only if you need custom update orchestration or don't need updates at all.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07) | human review v2 batch 3 (Youssef Zemzem, 2026-11-07): 'rolling updates' replaced with the documented 'declarative updates to Pods'

question: How do I run a batch job that must succeed 5 times, with 2 pods running at a time?

relevant.section: Jobs > Writing a Job spec

reference_answer: Set `completions: 5` and `parallelism: 2` in the Job spec.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: How do I have finished Jobs deleted automatically?

relevant.section: Jobs > Clean up finished jobs automatically

reference_answer: Set `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` on the Job; the TTL controller deletes it (and its Pods) that many seconds after it finishes.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: What happens when a PersistentVolumeClaim doesn't name a storage class?

relevant.section: Storage Classes > Default StorageClass
Dynamic Volume Provisioning > Defaulting Behavior

reference_answer: If the cluster has a default StorageClass, it's used to dynamically provision a volume for the claim.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: What are the Pod QoS classes and how does Kubernetes assign them?

relevant.section: Pod Quality of Service Classes > Quality of Service classes

reference_answer: Guaranteed (every container has equal CPU and memory requests and limits), Burstable (at least one request or limit, but not Guaranteed) and BestEffort (no requests or limits). The class influences eviction order under node pressure.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: How can important pods push out less important ones when the cluster is full?

relevant.section: Pod Priority and Preemption > PriorityClass
Pod Priority and Preemption > Preemption

reference_answer: Create a PriorityClass and set `priorityClassName` on the important Pods; when they can't be scheduled, the scheduler can preempt (evict) lower-priority Pods.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: What is a sidecar container and how is it different from an init container?

relevant.section: Sidecar Containers > Differences from init containers

reference_answer: Sidecars start before the app containers and keep running alongside them for the Pod's lifetime; init containers run to completion before the app starts.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: What does each part of the Kubernetes control plane do?

relevant.section: Kubernetes Components > Core Components

reference_answer: kube-apiserver exposes the API, etcd stores cluster data, kube-scheduler assigns Pods to nodes, kube-controller-manager runs the controllers; nodes run the kubelet, kube-proxy and a container runtime.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Can I make a ConfigMap read-only so nobody changes it by mistake?

relevant.section: ConfigMaps > Immutable ConfigMaps

reference_answer: Yes: set `immutable: true`. Its data can't be changed afterwards; delete and recreate it to change it.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: How can a container find out its own pod name and namespace?

relevant.section: Downward API > Available fields

reference_answer: Through the Downward API: expose `metadata.name` and `metadata.namespace` as environment variables (`fieldRef`) or as files in a `downwardAPI` volume.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Comment utiliser une image d'un registre privé qui demande une authentification ?

relevant.section: Récupération d'une image d'un registre privé > Créez un Secret en fournissant les identifiants sur la ligne de commande
Récupération d'une image d'un registre privé > Créez un Pod qui utilise votre Secret

reference_answer: Créer un Secret de type docker-registry (par ex. `regcred`) et le référencer dans `imagePullSecrets` du Pod.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Comment donner à un Pod un volume temporaire qui disparaît avec lui ?

relevant.section: Configurer un pod en utilisant un volume pour le stockage > Configurer un volume pour un Pod

reference_answer: Utiliser un volume `emptyDir`, qui existe tant que le Pod tourne sur le nœud.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Que se passe-t-il si un conteneur dépasse sa limite de mémoire ?

relevant.section: Allouer des ressources mémoire aux conteneurs et aux pods > Dépasser la limite de mémoire d'un conteneur

reference_answer: Il peut être arrêté (OOMKilled), puis redémarré selon la politique de redémarrage.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Comment définir une variable d'environnement pour un conteneur ?

relevant.section: Définir des variables d'environnement pour un Container > Définir une variable d'environnement pour un container

reference_answer: Ajouter un champ `env` avec `name` et `value` dans la spécification du conteneur.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Comment utiliser la valeur d'un Secret comme variable d'environnement ?

relevant.section: Distribuer des données sensibles de manière sécurisée avec les Secrets > Définir des variables d'environnement avec des Secrets

reference_answer: Dans `env`, utiliser `valueFrom.secretKeyRef` avec le nom du Secret et la clé.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Comment ouvrir un shell dans un conteneur en cours d'exécution ?

relevant.section: Obtenez un shell dans un conteneur en cours d'exécution > Obtenir un shell dans un conteneur

reference_answer: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- /bin/bash`.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Comment accéder depuis ma machine au port d'un Pod sans l'exposer ?

relevant.section: Utiliser le Port Forwarding pour accéder à des applications dans un cluster > Rediriger un port local vers un port du pod

reference_answer: `kubectl port-forward` vers le Pod, par ex. `kubectl port-forward pods/<nom> 28015:27017`.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07) | self-check: aligned with the referenced text

question: Quelles sont les classes de qualité de service (QoS) d'un Pod ?
reference_answer: Guaranteed, Burstable et BestEffort, attribuées selon les requests et limits de CPU et de mémoire des conteneurs.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Comment forcer un Pod à tourner sur un nœud qui porte un label précis ?

relevant.section: Assigner des pods aux nœuds > Ajouter un label à un nœud
Assigner des pods aux nœuds > Créez un pod qui sera planifié sur un nœud sélectionné.

reference_answer: Ajouter un label au nœud (`kubectl label nodes <nœud> disktype=ssd`), puis un `nodeSelector` correspondant dans le Pod.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Comment créer un autoscaler horizontal pour un déploiement ?

relevant.section: Découverte de l'HorizontalPodAutoscaler > Créer le HorizontalPodAutoscaler

reference_answer: `kubectl autoscale deployment php-apache --cpu-percent=50 --min=1 --max=10`.
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Comment voir l'état et les conditions d'un nœud ?

relevant.section: Noeuds > État du nœud

reference_answer: `kubectl describe node <nom>` ; l'état comprend notamment les conditions (Ready, MemoryPressure, DiskPressure…).
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)

question: Comment limiter l'accès à un Service aux seuls Pods qui portent un label précis ?

relevant.section: Déclarer une politique réseau (NetworkPolicy) > Limiter l'accès au Service `nginx`

reference_answer: Créer une NetworkPolicy qui sélectionne les Pods du Service et n'autorise l'ingress que depuis les Pods portant le label voulu (par ex. `access: "true"`).
notes: golden v2 draft (2026-11-07)
